comment: D-LOGO-11. Cases for logo_dimensions and logo_within_bounds in bin/omarchy-iptv, read by tests/test_logo_dimensions.py. Bytes are hex because .js and .py sources are ASCII only (CLAUDE.md rule 8); the cases are tiny real images from ImageMagick, some with their declared dimensions rewritten in the header, which is the whole point of the defect: the cost is quadratic in a number the bytes do not have to honour. dimensions is null where the header cannot be read, and withinBounds is then false, because a bound that cannot tell 'unreadable' from 'small' IS the defect (ruling R4).

cases.note: a real 64x64 baseline JPEG, untouched: the type must still be accepted
a real 64x64 progressive JPEG (SOF2), the shape the finding exploits at size
a real 64x64 PNG, untouched
a real 64x64 GIF, untouched: the block walk must reach the trailer
a real 64x64 lossy WEBP (VP8 keyframe), untouched
a real 64x64 lossless WEBP (VP8L), bit-packed dimensions
a real 64x64 extended WEBP (VP8X canvas + ALPH), the variant with a canvas
SOF2 rewritten to 20000x20000: the lead measured 840 MB peak RSS for 304 bytes
SOF0 rewritten to 65500x65500: the lead measured 455 MB; baseline is exposed too
IHDR rewritten to 20000x20000 with the CRC repaired: Qt refuses it today, the bound must not depend on that staying true (R3)
logical screen 65500x65500 with a real 64x64 frame: the canvas is the allocation
VP8 keyframe dimensions rewritten to the format maximum 16383x16383
a 300x200 frame whose marker is SOF3 (lossless). A reader narrowed to 0xC0..0xC2 answers None here and R4 turns that into a refusal of a real image
the same at SOF9, arithmetic-coded extended sequential: the second marker the narrow reader cannot see
a bomb hidden behind SOF3: the wide marker set must refuse it, not walk past it
a 120x90 canvas whose image descriptor declares 65500x65500. Whether Qt clips a frame to the canvas is unmeasured, so the answer is the maximum over both
4096x1024 is exactly MAX_LOGO_PIXELS and exactly MAX_LOGO_SIDE on one side: both comparisons must be <= and not <
4097x1024 is 4.19 Mpx, inside the pixel bound, and one pixel over the side bound
2048x2049 passes BOTH side checks and is 2,048 pixels over the area bound: the case that is only caught by the pixel comparison
2048x2048 is exactly MAX_LOGO_PIXELS as a square
4096x4096 sits exactly ON the side bound twice and is four times the area bound
65535x64 is 4,194,240 px, INSIDE the pixel bound, and is the shape the side cap is the second half of the rule for
the boundary is a property of the bound, not of the JPEG parser: PNG at 4 Mpx passes
PNG one pixel over the side bound
PNG inside both side bounds and over the area bound
GIF at exactly the area bound
GIF over the area bound with both sides legal
VP8L at exactly the area bound
VP8X canvas one pixel over the side bound
VP8L over the area bound with both sides legal
the SOI and nothing else: cannot tell, so refuse
the PNG signature and nothing else
a GIF header too short to hold the logical screen descriptor
RIFF....WEBP with no chunk at all
a JPEG cut off inside the SOF segment, after its length: the marker walk runs off the end and must answer None rather than reading past it
the signature plus a partial IHDR: 20 bytes, four short of the height field
a GIF whose block walk does not reach the trailer inside the bytes given
a WEBP whose first chunk header declares 142 bytes of body and carries 4

the PNG signature with a correctly-CRCd first chunk renamed gAMA. The parser reads IHDR by POSITION, so this is None: trusting a chunk's name rather than its place is how a crafted file gets a second opinion about its size
a JPEG whose frame header has been cut out, so the marker walk meets the scan first. There is no size to read and the answer must be None, not a guess
real PNG bytes handed in as image/jpeg: the JPEG reader must answer None rather than guessing, so a confused content type is a refusal
a content type outside LOGO_TYPES: no parser, so None
no bytes at all
a GIF declaring a 0x0 canvas and a 0x0 frame: a zero side is not an image, and 0 pixels would otherwise sail through both bounds

an APP1 EXIF segment carrying a whole 64x64 JPEG thumbnail, then a frame header declaring 20000x20000. A reader that hunts for the first SOF bytes instead of walking the segments reads the thumbnail's 64x64 and passes a bomb the probe took to 1,239 MB; the segment walk reads the frame
the same APP1 thumbnail in front of a real 64x64 frame: the segment walk must still accept an ordinary camera-style JPEG
64x65535 is 4,194,240 px, INSIDE the pixel bound, and over the side bound in HEIGHT only: the case a side check that forgot its second half passes
1024x4096 is jpeg-at-the-pixel-bound transposed: exactly MAX_LOGO_PIXELS, exactly MAX_LOGO_SIDE in height, and it passes
1024x4097 is one pixel over the side bound in height and inside the pixel bound
2049x2048 is 2,048 pixels over the area bound with both sides legal, the transpose of jpeg-one-over-the-pixels: an area computed as height squared answers 4,194,304 here and passes it
a 64x64 canvas whose FIRST image descriptor is 64x64 and whose SECOND declares 65500x65500. A walk that returns at the first descriptor reads 64x64 and passes it; the walk has to reach the trailer
PNG 64x65535: inside the pixel bound, over the side bound in height only
PNG 1024x4096: exactly the area bound with the side bound reached in height
PNG 1024x4097: one pixel over the side bound in height
PNG 2049x2048: both sides legal, 2,048 pixels over the area bound

a 64x64 canvas with THREE image descriptors: 64x64, 64x64, then 65500x65500. The second-frame case pins a walk that stops at the first descriptor; this one pins a walk that stops at the second, which a review found survived every test. The walk has to reach the trailer, whatever the frame count
